pages.text: The Inspector is a read-only window into a proof.$(br2)It shows the same directed graph that the server validates and executes. Selecting a node reveals its rune, output type, purity, formula, and cost.$(br2)The Inspector is a lens, not a second spell editor. It is not the future Advanced editing surface.

pages.title: Three kinds of motion
pages.text: Pure runes calculate from their inputs and may be normalized when every input is known. Observations read the world or an actor and remain dynamic. Effects cross the boundary into a world action.$(br2)A dynamic dependency is not an error; it is the part of the proof that waits for the world.

pages.title: Guided and inscribed
pages.text: The Laboratory stores a bounded sequence of Rune Form invocations. The Inscribed mode stores the authoritative ProgramGraph.$(br2)The Laboratory may reopen a saved proof only when replaying every invocation produces exactly the same graph. Missing forms never become a partial or guessed spell.

pages.title: Reading the canvas
pages.text: Layers show the direction of information flow. Lines connect a source output to a named input. Teal marks pure calculation, gold marks observation, and coral marks effects.$(br2)Click a node or move with the arrow keys. Close the Inspector to return to the Programmer; nothing is inscribed or consumed by inspection.
